reason: The Book of Esther, from which this fragment is drawn, is notably unique among Hebrew biblical texts in that it never explicitly mentions God (YHWH/Yahweh) by name or makes any direct statements about divine will or desires. The entire narrative focuses on human actors (King Ahasuerus, Esther, Mordecai, Haman) and political events in the Persian court. While the text does describe the Jews being delivered from destruction and subsequently thriving, this deliverance is presented as resulting from human agency and circumstance rather than from explicit divine action or stated divine will. The statement makes a claim about what Yahweh 'wants,' but no such statement appears in or is directly affirmed by the text.
